name: SubDL Scribe
description: SubDL Scribe brings SubDL.com to Jellyfin: it downloads missing subtitles for the languages and libraries you pick and uploads your own. Download is on by default; upload is off — enable at your choice. Requires a SubDL login and API Key plus a TMDb API Key.
overview: Sync subtitles with SubDL — download missing and upload new subtitles.

versions.changelog:
v12.1.12.167: The plugin no longer stops itself. The one limit left is SubDL's.
    A per-run hourly call bucket sat in our own code and could end a whole run when it
    filled up. SubDL publishes DAILY counters only, so that bucket was our invention, and
    it stopped runs the server would have allowed: in two measured runs 735 of 2000 searches
    and 16 of 50 downloads were still free when it fired. It is gone. What remains is the
    pacing - the gap between two transfers and the pause between calls - and the run stops
    only when SubDL itself says no (HTTP 429), decided against the live server counters.
    With it go the roll-over anchor and the "wait until the next hour" behaviour: a deferral
    now lands a plain job spacing after the stop, the same knob every other wait already uses,
    instead of a moving point an hour away that the settings page could not explain.
    The watchdog's grace no longer scales with the rate either. One file transfer is allowed
    five minutes, and the scaled value was shorter, so a slow but working download could be
    aborted as "frozen"; the grace is a fixed six minutes now.
    Smaller, same round: the call pause runs to 10 seconds instead of 5, and the rate field
    is labelled "Transfer rate" because that is what it is - a pace, not a ceiling.
    The quota box also names a local deferral and its cause and turns the bar yellow with it.
